note: BUG#38 (QualityControl ledger) — Ruby's EntityDispatchOrder runs ArgumentGate's refuse_unknown_arguments/refuse_absent_arguments BEFORE locate_element, so an entity command call carrying both an undeclared argument (colour) and a shape-mismatched declared one (id: a nested array where a scalar/`{value:}` identity is expected) always refuses UnknownArgument first, matching the established precedent (BUG#7/#8/#14/#19) that unknown-argument detection is the first DISPATCH_ORDER step. Rust's generated route-less entity-dispatch branch (rust/src/generated/chess/merged.rs's Piece.Capture arm, emitted by rust/project/domain_generator.rb + rust/project/registry.rb, mirrored in rust/codegen) used to extract the entity's own identity via Piece::extract_id BEFORE calling the generated PieceCaptureEntityArgs::from_json (where the unknown-argument check actually lives) — Piece::extract_id fails on the malformed nested-array id shape and raises TypeMismatch("Piece: no identity found (tried id.value, id, piece)") before from_json's own unknown-key check is ever reached, inverting Ruby's dispatch-order contract. Confirmed genuinely broken before this fixture existed: unmodified Rust answered TypeMismatch; Ruby always answered UnknownArgument ("Capture does not declare colour — it takes id, by"). Fixed via a standalone BUG#23-style structural precheck (unknown/absent-argument names only, no declared-argument type coercion) spliced INSIDE the route-less None arm of the entity/nested-entity dispatch match, before its own extract_id calls — deliberately narrower than moving the whole Args::from_json call earlier (a first attempt at this fix, reverted after it surfaced a separate, pre-existing bug where a single-attribute value object's own from_json checks for unknown keys before its own missing-field check, confirmed independently reproducible via a bare aggregate-creating command with no entity dispatch involved at all) and deliberately scoped to the None arm alone rather than the whole match (a second attempt, also reverted, incorrectly moved this ahead of an explicit route's own require_depth check too, refusing AbsentArgument instead of the wrong-depth TypeMismatch Ruby produces for an explicitly-routed call with a genuinely absent argument — confirmed live via qa/stress_domains/nested_pieces's Workspace.Board.AddCard with a scalar to: mutation). No setup steps needed: the malformed call refuses on its own declared-argument shape before ever needing a real Game/Piece to exist, on both engines.
